historical_references.reference: Elianora of Aquitaine (1122-1204) was the daughter of Duke William X of Aquitaine and Aenor of Châtellerault. She was married at a young age to Duke Leopold IV of Austria but the marriage was annulled due to consanguinity. Elianora then married King Louis VII of France and bore him a daughter, Marie-Louise, who later married Louis VIII of France. Elianora's third marriage was to King Alfonso II of Aragon in 1174, with whom she had a son, Jaime I. Elianora was a significant figure in the history of Europe during the Middle Ages, particularly due to her numerous marriages and her role in the political machinations of the period.

Elianora of Portugal (1438-1460) was a Portuguese princess, the only child of King Duarte of Portugal and his second wife, Leonor of Aragon. She was named after her grandmother, Queen Elianor of Aragon, who was a queen consort of King Alfonso XI of Castile. Elianora was engaged to King Edward IV of England in 1460 but she died before the marriage could take place. Her death marked the end of the House of Aviz in Portugal, as her only surviving brother, Afonso, had died earlier, leaving no direct heirs.
